answer: Night dispatch boards filled with twin radio handles that never left the lot. A route starts after the claimant flies a 90-gram falcon-lure on a 2.4 GHz path, records a 16-second RSSI trace at 8 Hz, and posts the 32-byte hash to a public beacon within 6 minutes, locking 36 POA in a meadow vault for 9 epochs. Five watchers must match the trace within 1.2 dB; peers re-hash the 128-sample file in 0.4 seconds. One key may fly 1 lure per epoch, so 80 aliases lock 2,880 POA. A reused lure hash, or two traces agreeing on 110 of 128 samples, burns 18 POA and bars that key from the beacon for 8 epochs.
